title: Implement role-aware shell, home, command/search, inbox and record anatomy
why_open: Bible §5.1 requires "Global command/search (⌘/Ctrl K) with permission-aware actions and recent objects". The tenant product has NO ⌘K at all: apps/web/src/components/shell/SearchCommand.tsx:118-127 is the only key handler in the whole shell and it is an onKeyDown on its own <input> handling ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Escape; `grep -rn "metaKey|ctrlKey" apps/web/src/components/shell apps/web/src/components/ui` returns zero hits, so the palette cannot be reached from the keyboard from any route. The OPERATOR app already has one — apps/system-studio/src/components/Launcher.tsx:5 ("GE-022-007. In the layout so Ctrl/Cmd-K reaches it from every route") + apps/system-studio/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx — so the deployer console has the tenant product's specified affordance and the tenant product does not. Second half missing: the palette returns only objects from /api/search (SearchCommand.tsx:16-23 `kind: memory|document|approval|event|organization`); there are no permission-aware ACTIONS and no RECENT OBJECTS, both named in §5.1. Third: the dropdown has no combobox semantics — SearchCommand.tsx:94 is `role="search"` on the form, the input at :107-134 carries only aria-label, and the results at :139-170 are a plain <div>/<ul>/<li>, so there is no role=combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant or role=listbox/option anywhere in the file. The `active` index at :121 moves a background colour only; a screen-reader user arrowing through results is told nothing. Record anatomy (§5.3) has no shared primitive either: apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/page.tsx is 10 lines that redirect straight to /members, so a record has no identity+status+primary-actions header at all.
smallest_real_change: In SearchCommand.tsx add a document-level keydown listener (useEffect) that focuses/opens the palette on (metaKey||ctrlKey)&&key==='k' and preventDefaults it, and give the widget real combobox semantics: input gets role="combobox", aria-expanded={showDropdown}, aria-controls="shell-search-listbox", aria-autocomplete="list", aria-activedescendant={active>=0?`shell-search-opt-${active}`:undefined}; the <ul> gets id + role="listbox"; each <li> gets id + role="option" + aria-selected. Feed permission-aware ACTIONS from the nav the layout ALREADY resolves — apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:64 computes `navSections` from navigationForSystem(institution.slug, capabilities); pass it into <ShellHeader sections={navSections}> → <SearchCommand actions={...}> so an action a user's capabilities do not grant can never be listed (do NOT put this in apps/web/src/lib/commands — that path belongs to another run). Consumers to fix in the same change: ShellHeader.tsx:36-45 props + apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:75-84 construction site (the new prop must be required, not optional, or the layout silently ships an action-less palette). Prove: jest DOM test rendering SearchCommand asserting aria-activedescendant tracks the arrowed row — mutation: delete the aria-activedescendant attribute from the input, test must red; restore, green. Plus a Playwright test in e2e/shell.spec.ts pressing Control+K from /dashboard and asserting the combobox is focused and expanded — mutation: remove the document keydown listener, test must red.

title: Implement safe tenant-brand overrides and rejection/preview
why_open: Two of the three clauses are absent. REJECTION: Bible §14 says "Automated contrast/gamut checks reject unsafe tenant tokens", but packages/platform-config/src/branding.ts:123-140 validates ONLY the syntax — `const safe = (value) => hexColor.safeParse(value).success` where hexColor (branding.ts:28-30) is `/^#(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{3}|[0-9a-fA-F]{6})$/`. A tenant setting primaryColor="#ffff00" against the default primaryTextColor="#ffffff" ships a 1.07:1 button, and nothing measures it: the contrast audit reads only the four STATIC themes out of the stylesheet (apps/web/src/lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts:26 GLOBALS_CSS, consumed by contrast.test.ts:225 "WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, in every theme"), and tenant CSS is injected after that at apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:70 via `brandingCss(brandingFor(institution.slug))`. SEMANTIC LEAK: Bible §4 says tenant branding "cannot override focus, danger, warning, success, security, disabled, selection or data-series semantic tokens" — but the focus ring is painted from the very token branding replaces: apps/web/src/app/globals.css:349-350 `[data-focus-visible] { outline: 2px solid var(--primary); }` and globals.css:480-481 `.chart-hit:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary); }`, plus focus rings hardcoded as `ring-[--primary]` in SearchCommand.tsx:103 and SideNav.tsx:146. globals.css:68 and :203 already declare a separate `--border-focus` per theme that brandingCss never writes, so the correct token exists and is simply not used. PREVIEW: none — apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx:95-98 offers only ThemeSwitcher (light/dark/system) and no branding surface exists anywhere in apps/web (`grep -rn "branding|primaryColor|wordmark" apps/web/src` finds only the layout call site and doc comments).
smallest_real_change: Do NOT edit packages/platform-config (owned by another run). Add apps/web/src/lib/a11y/tenant-brand.ts exporting `assessBrand(branding): {accepted: Branding, rejections: {token, ratio, floor}[]}` that uses the EXISTING contrast.ts (parseColor/composite/ratio) to measure primaryColor vs primaryTextColor (≥4.5:1) and primaryColor vs --surface (≥3:1 for the UI-component floor), dropping any failing value back to the platform default and returning the reason. Call it at the one production site: apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:70 becomes `brandingCss(assessBrand(brandingFor(institution.slug)).accepted)`. Separately close the semantic leak by repointing focus to the non-overridable token: globals.css:350 and :481 `var(--primary)` → `var(--border-focus)`, and the same substitution in SearchCommand.tsx:103 and SideNav.tsx:146 (grep `--primary` across src/components for any other focus ring before finishing — those four are the current set). Preview: a small server component components/brand/BrandPreview.tsx rendering the accent on button/nav/focus swatches in light, dark and high-contrast with the measured ratio and any rejection text, mounted in settings/page.tsx beside Appearance. Prove: jest test on assessBrand — mutation: change the floor from 4.5 to 0 and confirm the "rejects a low-contrast accent" case reds; restore. And a test asserting the value the PRODUCTION path emits — read globals.css and assert no `[data-focus-visible]` or `:focus-visible` rule resolves to a token brandingCss writes (--primary/--primary-hover/--primary-press/--primary-light/--primary-text) — mutation: put `var(--primary)` back on line 350 and confirm it reds.

title: Pass UI security/privacy/export/session/forbidden-state tests
why_open: The forbidden state is never rendered. apps/web/src/components/ui/StateSurface.tsx is a complete 150-line component that renders the fourteen states of states.ts (including `permission-denied`, `stale`, `partial`, `offline`) with the ARIA role and politeness read from the table — and it has ZERO production callers. Repo-wide `grep -rn StateSurface apps packages tests modules` returns exactly four sources: its own file, apps/web/src/components/ui/states.test.ts (its own fixtures), and one prose mention in Skeleton.tsx:20. It is a component proven only by a test that constructs it itself; no route reaches it. What routes do instead is call notFound() for CAPABILITY refusals on surfaces the person legitimately reached: apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/overrides/page.tsx:33 `if (!canEvent && !canContent) notFound()` and admin/audit/page.tsx:36 `if (!hasCapability(ctx, "audit.view", institutionId)) notFound()` — an administrator inside the console, who already knows the page exists (SideNav rendered the link), is told it does not. Bible §12 wants existence hidden from people who should not know it, which notFound() correctly does for OBJECTS (orgs/[slug]/documents/page.tsx:42), but a capability refusal on an already-visible surface is the `read-only`/`permission-denied` case states.ts:28-31 was written for. Session clause also open: apps/web/src/components/documents/DocumentViewerOverlay.tsx:98 holds the draft in `useState` with a SaveStatus of idle|dirty|saving|saved|error|conflict — there is no 401/expired branch, so an idle-expired session (SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS, apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:63) turns an autosave into a redirect and the draft is gone. Export clause is vacuous rather than failing: there is no CSV/print/download-with-classification path in apps/web at all (`grep -rli csv apps/web/src` finds only upload parsing and attachment chips).
smallest_real_change: Give StateSurface a real production caller and keep the existence rule intact. In admin/overrides/page.tsx:33 and admin/audit/page.tsx:36 replace `notFound()` with `return <StateSurface state="permission-denied" />` — both sit BEHIND admin/layout.tsx:19's `if (!isAdmin(ctx)) notFound()`, so the viewer is already known to be an administrator and no object existence is disclosed; leave every object-level notFound() (orgs/[slug]/documents/page.tsx:42, calendar/[id]/page.tsx:47, messages/[id]/page.tsx:90) exactly as it is. In DocumentViewerOverlay.tsx add a `session-expired` branch to SaveStatus: when the autosave fetch returns 401, keep the draft in state, stop retrying, and render StateSurface state="permission-denied" with a re-authenticate link that returns to the same URL — the draft is retained in memory only, no token or secret is written anywhere (tests/security/no-tokens-in-browser-storage.test.mjs stays satisfied). Prove with Playwright in e2e/admin-console.spec.ts: sign in as the director, revoke `audit.view` via the seeded role (or sign in as an admin persona lacking it), assert `[data-state="permission-denied"]` with role="status" is visible and that the words do not appear as a 404 — mutation: change the page back to notFound() and confirm the test reds; and a second mutation deleting `role={semantics.role}` from StateSurface.tsx:110 must red the role assertion. For the session case, a Playwright test that clears the session cookie mid-edit, triggers a save, and asserts the textarea still holds the typed text while the expired state is shown — mutation: drop the 401 branch and confirm the draft assertion reds.

title: Users complete work without module/navigation clutter
why_open: Nothing anywhere proves the menu is scoped to what a person can actually do, so the gate rests on an unmeasured claim. The two nav e2e assertions are apps/web/e2e/shell.spec.ts:45-57 (one persona, three section labels present, Settings pinned last) and apps/web/e2e/admin-console.spec.ts:15-26, which signs in as a plain member and asserts only that the /admin PAGE BODY is absent — it never asserts the member's side nav lacks the "Admin Console" link, and the positive assertion at admin-console.spec.ts:21 exists only for the director. apps/web/src/lib/authz/navigation-capabilities.ts:145 navigationCapabilitiesFor is exercised solely by navigation-capabilities.test.ts against hand-built AuthorizationWorld fixtures, so freezing it to `return new Set(Object.values(NAV_CAPABILITIES))` (navigation-capabilities.ts:52-55) leaves the rendered product untested and the entire suite green — exactly the mutate-the-producer failure. There is also no budget on the menu at all: modules/index.ts contributes nine nav entries across five sections (Administration/Overview/Community/Operations/Knowledge, modules/index.ts:170-721) and nothing stops a tenth, an eleventh and a sixth section from arriving one module at a time, which is the clutter this gate names.
smallest_real_change: Add one Playwright case to e2e/shell.spec.ts that reads the RENDERED nav for two seeded personas against the same database: sign in as Dana Whitfield (OSE director) and assert nav.getByRole('link', {name: 'Admin Console'}) and 'Reports' are visible; sign in as Maya Johnson (plain member) and assert both have count 0 while 'Calendar'/'Messages' remain visible — asserting on what the production path emits, not on navigationCapabilitiesFor's return. Mutation proof: make navigationCapabilitiesFor return `new Set(Object.values(NAV_CAPABILITIES))` unconditionally, run the spec, confirm the member assertion reds; restore, confirm green. Then extend tests/architecture/nav-hrefs-are-served.test.mjs (it already parses every nav entry out of modules/index.ts) with the clutter budget the gate needs: assert the section vocabulary is a closed set and that no section carries more than five entries, so a new module has to be placed rather than appended. Mutation: add a sixth section name to a manifest entry and confirm the test reds.

title: Implement design-system versioning, release notes, migration and deprecation
why_open: None of the four exists. `grep -rn "@deprecated" apps/web/src packages` returns zero hits across the whole repository; there is no CHANGELOG.md anywhere outside node_modules (`find . -maxdepth 3 -name CHANGELOG.md -not -path '*/node_modules/*'` is empty); there is no design-system or token package (packages/ holds audit, authorization, configuration, contracts, finops, identity, metadata, module-runtime, organization-model, platform-config, provisioning, releases, workflow — none of them ship a component or a token). packages/releases versions a TENANT SYSTEM, not the design system: packages/releases/src/release.ts:5-21 defines a release as "blueprint + modules + resolved configuration + org topology + policies, frozen and hashed". The token layer itself is unversioned prose — apps/web/src/app/globals.css:38-42 declares --primary/--primary-hover/--primary-press/--primary-light and nothing records that they ever changed, so the #1c8c5a → #198052 contrast fix (recorded only as a comment in packages/platform-config/src/branding.ts:33-36) reached every tenant with no version, no note and no migration. Bible §16 requires "One versioned token package, icon package, component library, chart library and page-pattern library". The only versioned thing near the design system is the eslint exception ledger (apps/web/eslint.config.mjs:60-68, DESIGN_TOKEN_EXCEPTIONS with `expires`), which governs escapes from the system rather than the system itself.
smallest_real_change: Add apps/web/src/components/ui/design-system.ts exporting (a) `DESIGN_SYSTEM_VERSION` semver, (b) `VERSIONS: readonly {version, tokenHash, notes, migration}[]` — release notes and migration text as required fields, not optional, so an entry cannot be added empty — and (c) `DEPRECATIONS: Record<exportName, {replacement, deprecatedIn, removeIn}>`. Give it two real consumers so it is not a declaration: (1) a jest test design-system.test.ts that recomputes the token hash from the REAL stylesheet using the existing themeTokens()/GLOBALS_CSS reader in src/lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts:26 and asserts it equals VERSIONS.at(-1).tokenHash — changing any --token in globals.css then reds CI until a version entry with notes and migration is added; (2) an ESLint rule in apps/web/eslint.config.mjs (the file already carries five custom no-restricted-syntax rules and a documented exception process) that reports any import of a name listed in DEPRECATIONS, with the message naming the replacement and the removeIn version. Prove: mutation A — change --primary in globals.css by one digit, run the jest test, confirm it reds naming the missing version entry, restore. Mutation B — add a throwaway export to DEPRECATIONS, import it from a component, run `npm run lint --workspace apps/web`, confirm the rule fires; remove.

title: Define separate tenant/deployer shells and prevent navigation/pattern leakage
why_open: The first clause is genuinely DONE and should not be rebuilt: apps/system-studio is its own Next app with its own layout (apps/system-studio/src/app/layout.tsx:28-36 masthead + <Nav/> + <Launcher/>), its own globals.css and its own components, apps/web has an entirely separate shell (components/shell/*), no package ships .tsx (`find packages -name '*.tsx'` is empty) and neither app imports the other (`grep -rn '\.\./\.\./\.\./\.\./' apps/*/src` is empty). The second clause — PREVENT leakage — is not enforced. The two guards that exist are narrower than the requirement: tests/security/operator-boundary.test.mjs:52-77 asserts only that no apps/web route gates on `isPlatformOperator`, and tests/security/operator-plane-content.test.mjs:57-68 asserts only that the Studio imports no Prisma client. Nothing forbids a UI import across the two apps, nothing forbids a control-plane destination appearing in the tenant menu, and control-plane code already lives inside the customer application by design — tools/ownership-map.mjs:44-52 lists apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/, apps/web/src/lib/system/, apps/web/src/lib/platform/ and apps/web/src/app/api/platform/ as owned by the control-plane domain. So the separation currently holds by convention, and the first shared shell component or operator nav entry would be caught by review or not at all.
smallest_real_change: Add tests/architecture/shell-separation.test.mjs in the shape the neighbouring guards already use (git grep survey + floor assertions so a broken reader fails instead of passing emptily), asserting three properties: (1) no file under apps/system-studio/src imports anything under apps/web/src and vice versa — by relative path or by workspace name; (2) neither app's shell imports the other's component directory, so the two navigations cannot converge on one file; (3) every nav entry parsed from modules/index.ts (the same parse tests/architecture/nav-hrefs-are-served.test.mjs already performs) points at a route apps/web serves and at no control-plane path prefix (/platform, /tenants, /api/platform). Floors: fail if the survey finds fewer than two app source roots or fewer than eight nav entries. Mutation proof: add `import { SideNav } from '../../../web/src/components/shell/SideNav'` to an apps/system-studio component, run the test, confirm it reds naming the file; remove it and confirm green. Then add a nav entry with href '/platform/cost' to a manifest, confirm property (3) reds; remove.
